### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/trigger-record-change`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/decouple-flow-record.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via RecordChangeTrigger (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via buildContext (symbol, a method of class RecordChangeTrigger))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/decouple-flow-record.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b4ee88fbc530a155ce3ea0570ad81d905d3afbb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `263425d70bfdae2a07837418e10d63b018804a09` — the merge of head `bbfe7cb244fb2ec1bf78aa15eb437d6b8093f9f8` into base `4b4ee88fbc530a155ce3ea0570ad81d905d3afbb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 263425d70bfdae2a07837418e10d63b018804a09 && git checkout 263425d70bfdae2a07837418e10d63b018804a09
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4b4ee88fbc530a155ce3ea0570ad81d905d3afbb bbfe7cb244fb2ec1bf78aa15eb437d6b8093f9f8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4b4ee88fbc530a155ce3ea0570ad81d905d3afbb && git merge --no-ff bbfe7cb244fb2ec1bf78aa15eb437d6b8093f9f8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b4ee88fbc530a155ce3ea0570ad81d905d3afbb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4b4ee88fbc530a155ce3ea0570ad81d905d3afbb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bbfe7cb244fb2ec1bf78aa15eb437d6b8093f9f8`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Read against `main` at the merge-base `91e8fa194` (stage 12's landing), board and tree read 2026-09-30T06:30Z. The PR's recorded base is `4b4ee88fb`; `origin/main` at this read is `7a09eee1b`, eight commits past the merge-base (`cd6d8a5ff`, `1bcba27d2`, `a3d7588b5`, `9ad654487`, `274e16271`, `085ca6bc1`, `4b4ee88fb`, `7a09eee1b`). None of the eight touches `packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/**`, this PR's changeset, `.changeset/config.json`, `scripts/check-issue-citations.mjs` or `scripts/doc-authoring-prose-id.baseline.json`, so the net diff against `main` is the merge-base diff, and the three-dot and two-dot numstats are byte-identical: 6 files, +40/−30 — 5 source files under `packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/**` (2 modules, 3 test files) and one changeset. The head repo is the base repo.

- **Accept-set: no change — right.** No Zod schema, REST handler, query-parameter set, refusal text, log text or runtime string moves. 30 source lines out, 30 in; every one of the 60 changed lines opens with a comment marker after whitespace (`//`, `*`, `/**`), 0 fall outside one. Each of the 5 touched files keeps its line count at the head (932, 219, 142, 861, 643), so no line citation into these files moves. The dev's parser leaf-token guard (0 files with a token change; both positive controls DIFFER) says the same and is not repeated here.
- **Public surface: no change — right.** No export added, removed or renamed; no `packages/spec` file touched, so no generated artifact is owed.
- **Published bytes: changed — right, and it decides ②.** `@objectstack/trigger-record-change` (17.5.0, not private, `files` = `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `types` = `dist/index.d.ts`, built by the root `tsup.config.ts` with `dts` on, then `check-dts-emitted`). `src/index.ts` exports `RecordChangeTrigger`, and the rewritten `buildContext` docblock (`record-change-trigger.ts:340-341`) is the leading comment of a member of that class, so the declaration emit carries the new text. The dev's A3 reading over all four `dist` entries, with positive and negative controls (the sha 3 times in each JS entry, 2 in each declaration file; no dead number left in `dist`), says the same; this record does not repeat the build.
- **The 3 numbers are dead — right.** `#14744`, `#13657` and `#11081` each answer 404 on the issues endpoint, read for this record; `#15356` and `#8738`, the only two numbers kept on added lines, answer 200. No ADR, `scripts/adr-anchors/` file or ruling record names any of the three as its decision (the dev's grep; the one `docs/` page naming `#14744` is the census record, which calls itself measurement only), so ruling C's first rung is empty and a commit is the right anchor for every one.
- **The 4 anchors — each right.** Each abbreviated sha resolves to exactly one commit (`rev-parse --disambiguate`, count 1 for all 4) and each is an ancestor of the merge-base (`merge-base --is-ancestor`, exit 0 for all 4). `git blame` at the base was run over every changed line: the 25 lines in `before-update-flow-payload-reach.test.ts`, `decouple-flow-record.test.ts`, `decouple-flow-record.ts` and `record-change-trigger.ts` were all written by `4f85e4d11`, and the 5 lines in `record-change-integration.test.ts` were all written by `c28e4cfae`.
  - `#14744` → `4f85e4d11` (the squash of PR #15475, "decouple the flow-facing record from the batch payload") on 22 lines. Its diff names `#14744` on 29 added lines; it created `decouple-flow-record.ts` and both pin test files; its changeset records the option-A ruling on `#14744` (decision batch #38, verbatim 「同意」) and states that the `#14099` key-set refusal "is untouched and is not widened — a hook that assigns the same key with per-row values still passes it". That is the decision each of the 22 rewritten sentences states.
  - `#14744` → `03c1b0f6f` (the squash of PR #15301) on the one line that describes the census, `before-update-flow-payload-reach.test.ts:29`. Its message names `#14744` five times (the PR body says four — a miscount, immaterial) and states the result the line quotes, "ZERO across 23 production registration sites". Its diff adds `docs/audits/2026-09-multi-update-per-row-value-census.md`, whose `:308-311` (blamed to this commit) hold the "a reading, not a measurement" conclusion the rewritten `:34` now places "in that census". It is an ancestor of `4f85e4d11`, which wrote `:29`. Per-line anchoring is the per-arm precedent this thread already carries (stage 5, `5895973934` item 2; stage 9, `5901366770`).
  - `#13657` → `b003cf2e8` (the squash of PR #13864, the post-hook half of the declared-field door). Its message names `#13657` seven times; it is an ancestor of `4f85e4d11`, which wrote `:206`. The pairing left on that line is right: `#8738` (live, closed by PR #8775, the door placed before the `beforeUpdate` hooks) is the pre-hook half, `b003cf2e8` the post-hook half.
  - `#11081` → `c28e4cfae` (the squash of PR #11570). Its message names `#11081` and its diff adds exactly the five `[#11081]` tags in `record-change-integration.test.ts`; blame puts all five lines in it. Stage 7's anchor for the same number.
- **The wordings — each right.** `:10` names the option-A ruling in words beside the commit whose changeset records it (the form stages 2, 6 and 7 used). `:22` and `:87` say the residue shape is what `4f85e4d11` pins: the positive control is in the test file that commit created. `:455` says the blind spot is what `4f85e4d11` "left unguarded": its changeset says the key-set refusal is untouched and not widened. `:29` and `:34` (the census, and the conclusion recorded in it) are checked above. `:686`, `:705`, `:738` and `:924` ("before commit 4f85e4d11 … read …") state the pre-fix readings the commit's own flip of `S5`, `S5b` and the SQL replica reversed. `:206` is checked above. `:23`, `:47`, `:95`, `:642`, `record-change-trigger.ts:124`, `:340-341`, `:453` and `:496` swap the number for the commit in a sentence that already states what the commit did.
- **Citation accounting — right.** Over the diff: the 30 removed lines carry `#14744` ×23, `#11081` ×5 and `#13657` ×1 (29 dead sites on 29 lines) plus the live `#15356` ×3 and `#8738` ×1; the added lines carry exactly `#15356` ×3 and `#8738` ×1, each on the line it already stood on. No number is new to an added line, none grew, no `PR #N` stands on an added line, and 4 distinct shas stand on added lines: `4f85e4d11` on 22 lines, `c28e4cfae` on 5, `03c1b0f6f` on 1, `b003cf2e8` on 1 — 29 rewritten lines, plus the one referent line (`:34`), which is the thirtieth.
- **The 4 sites left — right, and the list is exact.** A grep of the three numbers over `trigger-record-change/src` at the head returns exactly 4 lines: `before-update-flow-payload-reach.test.ts:825` (an `it` title), `:872` (a `describe` title, the second number of `[#15356/#14744]`), `decouple-flow-record.test.ts:78` and `:136` (`describe` titles). All four are string tokens, left as stages 1 to 12 left theirs. No operator string, assertion message, generated header or quoted ruling under `src` carries a dead number.
- **The gate-invisible spellings — right.** At the head under `src`: `#N-word` 0; `#A/#B` 5 lines (`before-update-flow-payload-reach.test.ts:118` `#4127/#4251`, `:872`, `bulk-write-per-row-context.test.ts:53` `#4127/#4251`, `:188` `#4862/#5038`, `record-change-trigger.ts:388` `#1871/#4649`), of whose second numbers only `#14744` is dead and it stands in the kept title; `option #N` 0; URL-spelled 0. The claim's 0 / 5 / 0 / 0.
- **Form — consistent with the landed stages 1 to 12** (`422db788a` … `91e8fa194`): the word `commit` plus the abbreviated sha where the number stood, the decision carried in the sentence. The two reuses this thread can check, `#13657` → `b003cf2e8` and `#11081` → `c28e4cfae`, are the anchors the earlier stages named for the same numbers.
- **Check-runs on the head, the gate verdicts,** read 2026-09-30T06:30Z: 34 check-runs, all completed — 31 `success`, 3 `skipped` (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`: paths-filtered or opt-in, not verdicts against), 0 failure. Every one of the seven required contexts is `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check:issue-citations` and `check:doc-authoring`, the two gates this diff answers to), `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (all six shards `success`), `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue` and `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` are `success`. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/20596-trigger-record-change-provenance-anchors.md` declares `'@objectstack/trigger-record-change': patch` — **matches what the diff publishes.** The package is released and its `dist/index.d.ts` carries the rewritten `buildContext` docblock, so bytes ship; `skip-changeset` would be wrong (it is for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package), and the PR carries no such label (`documentation`, `size/s`, `tests`, `tooling`, the labeler's). Not `minor`: no accept set widens and no surface is added. The body is stage 12's word for word except the package name (a diff of the two files changes exactly the two lines that name it), is truthful (comments only; no type, schema, export, log or refusal text, or runtime behaviour change), carries no tracker number and no model identifier, and the filename carries the card number. The package sits in the `fixed` group (`.changeset/config.json:51`) beside the eleven packages whose stage changesets are still in `.changeset/` on `main`, all declaring the same level.
- **`Clause-②: no` — right.** It is line 2 of the PR body under `Part of #20596`, and the claim (`5904332626`) declares the same. The diff widens no accept set, so no arm is owed and no `minor` is owed. Nothing breaks, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed; `Check Changeset` on the head is `success`.
- Not a governed-surface diff (no path under `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`); 70 changed lines, under the 5,000-line human-merge threshold; head repo equals base repo; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` on the head is `success`. A draft with `Part of` on line 1 and no closing keyword anywhere in the body, so the card stays open for the remaining stages.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report (`5905231194`) has `open_questions: []`. Its twelve deviations and three out-of-scope findings, each answered, then one reading of this record's own:

1. 23 test-comment sites beyond the census's 6, five of them `#11081` which the census never judged — **answered, in scope.** The claim's surface is comment and docblock prose under `trigger-record-change/src/**`; test comments are that, and stages 1 to 12 rewrote theirs. `#11081` answers 404 on this record's own read, and the head grep above confirms the residue is titles only.
2. `#14744` takes two anchors, per line — **answered, right** (① above). The census line cites the census commit and the 22 fix lines cite the fix; form C applied per line rather than per number, the per-arm precedent of stages 5 and 9 on this thread.
3. One changed line with no dead number (`before-update-flow-payload-reach.test.ts:34`), landed as its own commit `bbfe7cb24` — **answered, right.** Its referent moved with `:29`; the census record `03c1b0f6f` landed carries the conclusion the line now points at (`:308-311`, blamed to that commit). Line count unchanged; the head's check-runs are on this commit.
4. Wordings beyond the tag swap — **answered, right** (① above). Each was checked against its anchor commit's message, diff or changeset.
5. The supplementary instrument judged by stage 6's method (the before census's board reading, the gate's own extraction, single-number reads) — **answered, immaterial here.** A process note; the head grep of the three numbers is the residue check this record reads, and it is exact.
6. The harness attribution reminder versus the repo's trailer pair — **answered, right.** All three head commits (`bb9d39a87`, `bf03049f3`, `bbfe7cb24`) end with the model-free trailer pair AGENTS.md prescribes (the session-URL trailer and the plain co-author trailer), no model identifier appears in any message, and the PR body's footer is the session-URL form. AGENTS.md is the repo's rule, and the reminder itself defers to it.
7. No pre-PR merge; `main` moved past the base — **answered, right.** Verified above at eight commits: none touches a path in this diff or an input the citation gate derives from. The three roster inputs that moved (`engine-double-contract.pinned.json`, `objectql-double-limit.baseline.json`, `sdui-manifest.record.json`) cannot interact with a diff that moves no code token, and the merge queue rebuilds on the merged generation.
8. A scratch eslint probe placed, run and deleted in one command — **answered, immaterial.** The head tree holds no such file (`git ls-tree -r`, 0 hits).
9. Three census enumerations rather than two — **answered.** More evidence, not less; the final one is on the head.
10. Labels — **answered.** The labeler's four; no `skip-changeset`, which is right.
11. The PR body read back through the API but not byte-compared — **answered, immaterial.** The body as this record read it is complete: every section present, one footer, `Part of #20596` line 1, `Clause-②: no` line 2.
12. Worktree cleanup after the report — **answered.** A process note with no bearing on the head.
13. Out-of-scope 1, `record-change-trigger.ts:239`'s operator `warn` ending in `#3457` — **answered.** The number is live; form D, already held by the shrink-only `scripts/doc-authoring-prose-id.baseline.json` (`record-change-trigger.ts`: `#3457: 1`), so `check:doc-authoring` sees no growth. Carrier: the runtime-string lane.
14. Out-of-scope 2, 「the card」 on 3 comment lines in 2 files — **answered, verified at the head.** `before-update-flow-payload-reach.test.ts:865` sits under the heading at `:859`, whose surviving number `#15356` is the card whose consequence the line names (one SET clause, issued once, landing on every row — that card's own text), so the referent stands; `reentrant-start-condition.test.ts:14` and `:302` are untouched by this diff. Wording only.
15. Out-of-scope 3, `docs/audits/**` names the dead `#14744` on 8 lines in 2 files — **verified at the head; escalated to its carrier, not to this PR.** `docs/` is outside every stage of this card, and the census file names the number as its own subject. A dead citation in an audit record is documentation rot, not a defect or contract violation. Its carrier is #20556 (dead citations outside `packages/spec/src`), where stage 2's record already sent an ADR finding of the same class; the seat should leave a pointer there on its next write, with `03c1b0f6f` as the anchor already checked here. Nothing for the dev.
16. **This record's own reading, not in the PR body or the report:** `packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/tsconfig.test.json:54` carries `[#11081]` in a `//` comment (the line explaining why `rootDir` is widened). It is outside the claim's file surface (`src/**` only), outside the census's declared surface (`packages/**/src/**/*.{ts,tsx}`), and not in `files[]`, so it neither ships nor moves any gate, and leaving it is not a breach of the dispatch. It is a dead citation in this package all the same, and the body's outside-`src` inventory (which lists the shipping files only) does not name it. Escalated as a pointer, not as a flag on this PR: the carrier is this card's thread, for the seat's landing note or a later stage in this lane, with `c28e4cfae` as the anchor already checked here — its message names `#11081` and names this very `rootDir` widening. Not blocking.

Nothing else is escalated.
